subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack expose an opt-in `ignoreSubtypes` config for edit/delete events, or should OpenClaw keep or change the default edit/delete system-event policy without a new config key?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix adds public config and decides whether edit/delete events are useful system context or should be suppressible/no-op noise.

options.title: Add opt-in config
options.body: Expose a narrow Slack subtype ignore list and keep current behavior as the default, minimizing upgrade surprise while solving noisy workspaces.

options.title: Drop edit/delete by default
options.body: Treat edit/delete events as non-triggering everywhere, which is simpler but can remove system-event context for existing users.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Leave edit/delete events as system events and rely on prompts or future broader event-policy design instead of adding config now.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in config
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow Slack subtype ignore list and keep current behavior as the default, minimizing upgrade surprise while solving noisy workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history on Slack system-event ingress and the current subtype event policy.
